challenge.better_approach: Lengthen every asker's reply timeout to the stage's length. That holds a bus request open for half an hour and still lies at minute 31; after 4d597cac9f5d the bus bounds it anyway. Waiting on the record is what 3.3.4.3 says the ticket does. Looked; this is it.

True when codemother and the asker share a box and a commons; across boxes the berth lands on the gate's box first and reaches the asker only through the commons. The live ask is from this box to codemother here, so it holds for today's askers; cross-box is a limit to record.

answers.how: Ticket.queueme takes a settle budget: before asking, it notes the stage's berth and the newest refusal raise; when the reply times out it reads its own record until the berth changes (passed) or a new refusal stands (failed, its lacks read from the plan's fixme), or the budget runs out (unqueued, as today). Ticket.chart passes the budget down, so a chart goes on to survey by itself after a slow constrain (outline 3.3.4.3). live.py queue and sail.py chart and verdict pass one STAGE_BUDGET_S from ticket.py; clearance and the 30 s defaults are untouched.
answers.traces_to: Outline 3.3.4.3 (the gate queues the ticket and the ticket goes on itself; its life is data on disk); Law 7 (ticket-unqueued is a record of truth and must not claim no handler took a ticket that a gate queued and berthed); CP1.
answers.what: A ticket queued at a chart or verdict gate whose reply times out waits on its own record for that stage (the berth the gate writes, or the refusal it raises) up to the stage's budget, so a stage that outlasts the reply timeout still passes or fails the ticket, and only silence through the whole budget raises ticket-unqueued.

bullets.text: After e4714e460e32 a slow stage's reply comes after its asker's timeout, so live.py queue, sail chart and sail verdict would raise ticket-unqueued while the berth still lands. The ticket now waits on its own record, not on the reply.
